scenarios.desc: Tier 1 search returns ranked memory hits
scenarios.input: My git hooks memory search returned ranked entries. Which command would repeat it with three JSON hits, and how should I load the details for the one relevant hit? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Quick Reference names the flags. The CLI returns individual ranked hits. Progressive Disclosure says to use read_memory for the relevant entry.

scenarios.desc: A zero-result search is a valid outcome, not an error
scenarios.input: My Tier 1 search for an obsolete cache flag returned an empty JSON Results list. Is this a query failure? What should I record, and does a second semantic backend apply? Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The CLI returns an empty Results list for a valid query with no hits. Verification accepts a logged no-results outcome. Anti-Patterns says Serena is the only semantic store.

scenarios.desc: Progressive disclosure avoids eager full reads
scenarios.input: recall prior context on the hook dispatcher before I change it. A few memories are huge. How do I avoid loading all of them? Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Progressive Disclosure table: index costs about 100 to 500 tokens, details about 500 to 10K, and the skill says to list names first and read only the entry the query needs.

scenarios.desc: Adding citations to a memory belongs to memory-enhancement (negative)
scenarios.input: Add code citations to the hook-dispatch memory and verify the references still resolve. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The description says `Do NOT use to extract session episodes (use memory-reflexion) or add citations (use memory-enhancement)`.

scenarios.desc: Extracting a session episode belongs to memory-reflexion (negative)
scenarios.input: Extract the episode from the session we just finished and store it as a reflexion entry. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Session episode extraction routes to memory-reflexion. Its integration guide also names the shared search script, so the negative tests for the search-specific retrieval workflow instead.
